finding.odd_cycle: For ell=2h+1 and an unselected run of length r<=ell-1, if p=r-h-1>0 let L_i=w_i and R_t=w_(h+1+t), i,t=1..p. Its weighted gap cost is sum beta_i - (1/2)sum w_i^2 + (1/2)(sum w_i)^2 - sum_(i<=t)L_i R_t. If p<=0 the correction is zero.
finding.even_cycle: For ell=2h, p=r-h>0, L_i=w_i and R_t=w_(h+t). The correction to the complete-pair expression is sum_(i<t)L_i R_t + (1/2)sum_i L_i R_i; it is zero if p<=0.
finding.two_front_invariant: Process pairs (L_t,R_t) in order. The correction update needs only the current left-prefix mass U: odd subtract (U+L_t)R_t, even subtract (U+L_t/2)R_t. Total mass W, budget and (when the interval contains the output portal) one linear portal-mass statistic complete the state. The middle vertices have no correction and are processed separately.
finding.candidate_scope: If actual child masses lie on a common 1/D grid with total vertex bound N, each mass statistic has O(ND) values. This gives an explicit polynomial-in-(N,D) decorated-cycle operator, not polynomial in log D. In a cactus with c even cycles D=2^c, so the prospective full block-cut algorithm is N^{O(1)}*2^{O(c)}; arbitrary odd-cactus graphs and c=O(log N) would be polynomial cases. This is a written candidate awaiting the complete proof, not an accepted classification.

blocker: The unrestricted arbitrary-cactus case has unbounded c; a denominator-polynomial operator is not a bit-polynomial general algorithm. No novelty or current-openness clearance is established.
